outcome: Guest, payment and corporate traffic separated behind one inspecting boundary that blocks and logs intrusion attempts across every property.
overview: Hotel networks grow by addition — a guest wireless network here, a property-management system there, payment terminals added when the acquirer asked — and they end up flat, so anything that reaches the guest network can reach the systems that take card payments. FortiGate places an inspecting boundary between those zones and applies intrusion prevention and encrypted-traffic inspection at it, which turns an implicit trust relationship into an explicit, logged one. For a hospitality group the immediate driver is usually the payment-card audit; the durable gain is that a compromised guest device stops being a route to anything else.

benefits.text: Guest, payment and corporate traffic are separated by an inspecting boundary rather than by convention
benefits.limits: Segmentation only holds where the traffic actually crosses the boundary; a flat switch fabric behind it can still allow lateral movement the firewall never sees

benefits.text: Payment-card scope is reduced to a defined zone that can be evidenced to an assessor
benefits.limits: Scope reduction is the assessor’s determination, not the product’s; the design supports the argument and does not make it

benefits.text: Threats blocked at the boundary are logged, so an incident has evidence rather than inference
benefits.limits: The same operating system runs on the appliance, as a virtual machine and in cloud, so the capability claim survives a form-factor change; the throughput figure behind it does not, and must be re-sized per form factor

residency: Appliances and their logs stay on property, in the group data centre, or — where a virtual appliance is used — in the group’s own AWS or Azure account; no guest or cardholder traffic needs to leave the estate for inspection

notFor.situation: A property already segmented behind another vendor’s next-generation firewall
notFor.why: A second inspecting boundary in the same slot adds a rule base to maintain and no capability the first one lacks

notFor.situation: A single property with no payment or corporate systems on the same network
notFor.why: There is no trust boundary to place, so the platform has nothing to enforce between

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Fortinet implementation partner · Duration: 6–10 weeks for the first property and the template; subsequent properties on a repeatable pattern
Support model: Vendor hardware and subscription support with an agreed replacement term; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed policy operations.
1) Assessment — zone discovery, traffic profiling, rule-base analysis and throughput sizing
2) Design — zone model, rule set, decryption policy and the property template
3) Build — first property cut over, central management and logging established
4) Roll out and hand over — remaining properties on the template, operations handed over
deliverables: Traffic between any two zones is observed crossing the boundary and matching a named rule
The decryption policy states, per category, what is inspected and what is excluded and why
A policy change authored centrally reaches every property without per-site editing
effort: 6–10 weeks for the first property and the template; subsequent properties on a repeatable pattern
